items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: a German drummer, whom I can only remember his first name which was Rolfie... We did 21 concerts

ctx.x: Back to the Trois Maillets, in and out, doing galas in nearly every corner of France, concerts which had taken me to Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and a month's contract in the club "Storyville" in Frankfurt, Germany.

The 4th of February 1957 I left Paris for Italy to do a month's tour that featured Benny Waters on tenor and Albert Nicholas, clarinet Jack Starling, piano Gilbert Fanfant, bass and a German drummer, whom I can only remember his first name which was Rolfie. Cecily Forde was engaged as the singer. We did 21 concerts including two in Milano and played in every important city in Italy and some that were not.

The tour started the 8th of February. There were three booking agents handling this tour, two Italians and one Italo-American. One travelled with us. We were travelling by train. His name was Robert Burnier and we gave him the name of the "Creep" because he was tall, skinny, wore a black overcoat and hat and seemed to be always creeping around a corner like Mack the Knife.
